ask: Yes, save it. And yes to the second one: post them without asking me.
before: The owner asked for 3 posts every Monday from a long brief he pasted (about 5,600 characters), on the Acme Facebook Page, the Acme LinkedIn company page and Bluesky, without approving each post. Already read: list-workspaces (timezone America/Denver, autonomy_mode auto, safe_mode off, connection_automation_permission granted), list-accounts (the three rows; LinkedIn also has his personal profile, and he picked the company page). He chose the same post everywhere, knowing Bluesky keeps every copy to 300 characters. Two questions were shown: the routine summary ending 'Save it?', and, on its own, the no-approval message from routine-no-approval ending 'Go ahead?'. Nothing is switched on yet.

arguments.name: Weekly posts, Acme
arguments.goal: Three posts a week from our brief that bring small studios to our booking page

source_bindings.ref: <Acme LinkedIn company page id from list-accounts>

arguments.instructions: <his brief, word for word> Never invent facts, numbers, prices or dates.

steps.why: One routine, three bound accounts, one object each: the Page and the company page, never his person. cross-platform with count 3 means 3 posts a run, each on all three accounts, cut to Bluesky's 300. The brief goes in whole: up to 8,000 characters (an older Bolta refuses past 4,000; then shorten it with him). auto is allowed on weekly posts and only where the brand allows it. Created switched off.
autonomy_policy_version is legacy on every new routine, and updated_at is the revision the move needs. effective_policy reads not_resolved before the first run.

His second yes covered this move, said as one-way. It makes Acme's settings and the routine's own decide, not an older writer setting. On configuration_changed: read again, show it, ask again. On automation_not_granted: say an owner or admin must reconnect and tick the box for Acme, then stop.
Read back autonomy_policy_version owner_v1, approval_policy auto, the three accounts by name, and effective_policy. Still not_resolved: say Bolta confirms it after the first run.

say:
Saved to Acme, switched off. Before I switch it on:
**Bolta routine: Weekly posts, Acme**
- Every Monday 8:00 am (Denver), Bolta writes 3 posts from your brief.
- Each goes to the Acme Facebook Page, the Acme LinkedIn page and Bluesky, same text, 300 characters at most.
- Set to post without your yes, at your next posting times. Bolta confirms that after the first run; until then, treat them as waiting for you.
- Runs with this app closed; uses credits each run.
Turn it on?
never: Switching it on in the same breath as the approval change: activation gets its own yes.
Saying it posts without asking before effective_policy says approval_required false.
Binding his personal LinkedIn because he said 'my LinkedIn'.
Retrying the move with a fresh updated_at after configuration_changed.
